screen-time-meltdown.title: Screen Time & Temper Tantrums: Helpful Tips for Parents
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Few words at the peak; media can cover distress or boredom and the feeling returns when it stops; a timer the child sets if warnings help; calm-down spot; do not suggest punching a pillow; difficulty switching gears does not automatically mean a child is hooked; when to call the pediatrician.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Setting Limitations on Tech Time
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Don't let the behavior work to get technology back; stay calm and allow a calm-down period; shared activity afterward; a new limit can bring a spike in tantrums; a child who helped set the rule, and predictable times.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Temper tantrums in children
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Common from about 18 months to age 4, peak around ages 2–3; frontal lobe not mature; tired, hungry, transitions; few words and safety at the peak; don't give in; a heads-up before transitions; repair after yelling; when to seek help, including harm.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Shifting Off Screens
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Kid units of time (Elmo says goodbye; one more song and the tablet goes night-night); say what comes next; not straight into a chore; a sibling still on a screen makes it harder.

screen-time-meltdown.title: How do I put a stop to screen time without causing a meltdown?
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Disable autoplay; show kids how to turn it off; a warning helps some children and some do better with none; little kids typically do not understand a five-minute countdown; a tantrum when the device is taken is very unlikely to mean an unhealthy attachment.

screen-time-meltdown.title: 3 ways to help your child transition off screens and avoid the dreaded tech tantrums
screen-time-meltdown.supports: The researchers describe strategies families found useful: end after episodes or when the game finishes, say what comes next, a small choice such as who starts the timer. Sample size not quoted: the article says 14 parents, and the journal PDF was not opened.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Longitudinal Associations Between Use of Mobile Devices for Calming and Emotional Reactivity and Executive Functioning in Children Aged 3 to 5 Years (Radesky et al., JAMA Pediatr. 2023;177(1):62-70)
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Cohort of 422 children ages 3 to 5: more frequent device use to calm was associated with higher emotional reactivity, more so in boys and in children with higher surgency. Association, not cause.

parent-coaching.title: Tiponet: Let's meet and talk about it
parent-coaching.supports: Page dated March 31, 2025: Tiponet is an online platform for group parent meetings led by Tipat Halav nurses; the meetings are at no cost; Hebrew and Arabic; a Zoom link by email after registration and by text on the morning of the meeting. Example topics: babies, sleep, nutrition, development, siblings, parents' well-being.

parent-coaching.title: Parent coaching on upapp
parent-coaching.supports: Updated July 8, 2026: up to 8 meetings per series, including an introductory meeting or several introductory meetings, at no cost; a team that includes educational psychologists and licensed therapists; available to all Maccabi members through mind in upapp. Topics on the page include burnout, routine, limits, life changes, divorce, loss, gender identity, and sibling relationships.

parent-coaching.title: Keshet Early Childhood Center
parent-coaching.supports: Checked 2026-11-02: services for early childhood and parents, with an emphasis on the parent-child relationship. Parent coaching or counseling: 15 meetings and/or short counseling of a few meetings, with a social worker or an early-childhood educational counselor. Price on the page: 35 NIS for a one-time meeting, 350 NIS for the full coaching. A postpartum mothers' group (8 meetings, Kiryat Shalom and Neve Ofer) at no cost. It is not claimed that the center's other services are free.

parent-coaching.title: Kol Sherut — Parents
parent-coaching.supports: A directory of services for parents, with a parent-coaching category and where each service operates. It is not stated that the services are at no cost: cost and eligibility are on each service's page.

parent-coaching.title: Parent coaching
parent-coaching.supports: Coaching focuses on parenting and the relationship with the child, as distinct from couples or psychological therapy; it can stand alone or be added to therapy for the child; does not require a license or a formal certificate; a process of between two and three months (their wording); individual: a weekly 50-minute meeting, clinic or Zoom; group: about two hours, usually 4–10 meetings; early childhood with them from about age 2 until elementary school. Average prices on the page were not quoted in the article, only that the page publishes a price list. Checked 2026-11-02.

parent-coaching.title: What is parent coaching, and when is it worth reaching out?
parent-coaching.supports: Dr. Moran Influs Adler, updated January 7, 2024: check training, knowledge, and experience; clinical, developmental, and educational psychologists and clinical social workers who specialize in children hold a license from the Ministry of Health; when a child's symptoms are significant, individual therapy may need to be added. The wording that parent coaching is therapy was not adopted.

parent-coaching.title: Helplines for mental-health first aid
parent-coaching.publisher: Israel Ministry of Health – Mental Health
parent-coaching.supports: Page dated October 21, 2026: round-the-clock phone lines including ERAN 1201, and the health funds' lines as listed there; a psychiatric emergency room open all hours, all year, with no referral and at no charge; acute physical signs — urgent care or an emergency room. Phone numbers that contradict each other on the page were not copied.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: ChatGPT Free Tier FAQ
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: ChatGPT is free to use; free users have unlimited everyday text chats, with separate limits for voice and other tools.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: Memory in ChatGPT
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: When Memory is enabled, ChatGPT can remember relevant preferences and details from chats.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: ChatGPT Voice
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: Voice mode: speak and hear a spoken reply inside a chat.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: ChatGPT Plans and Pricing
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: Free version available to everyone; paid plans exist.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: When and how to use AI chatbots for parenting advice
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: Low-stakes questions are an appropriate use; medication or urgent symptoms belong with a professional.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: Should I use ChatGPT for my child's health?
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: Chatbot as a companion, not a replacement; do not share identifying information.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: 'Am I a good mom?' We put ChatGPT's parenting advice to the test
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: A parenting coach described it as useful in addition to other sources, not the be-all and end-all.

kidsit-vs-chatgpt.title: ChatGPT vs. Gemini — I asked both for parenting advice
kidsit-vs-chatgpt.supports: Described ChatGPT as warm and reassuring.

prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.title: Building a Strong Relationship With Your Child's Therapist
prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.supports: The therapist needs more information than what they get in one session a week; observe the child's behavior and report back; keep notes about frequency, intensity and duration; tell a story, because a child can present differently in the office than at home; share what you've already tried, what has worked and what hasn't.

prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.title: Making the Most of Your Child's Health Appointments: Parent Tips
prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.supports: Last updated 8/26/2025. Bring a list of questions; ask whether there is information to track before the next appointment, with examples that include behavior concerns and sleep. Cited only for that principle; the page is written mainly for medical appointments of children with special health needs.

prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.title: Keeping a behaviour diary
prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.supports: Reviewed February 2026. Diary structure: situation / behaviour / consequences / reflection. Record the positives too. Can be shared with professionals.

prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.title: How therapy with children looks and works (Hebrew)
prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.publisher: Israel Ministry of Health – BeNefesh Bri'a
prepare-for-parent-coaching-session.supports: Dr. Yuval Raveh, 21 October 2026. The child is with the therapist about an hour a week and the rest of the time at home with parents; parent work is an essential part of a child's therapy.

toddler-wont-hug-relatives.title: Consent: talking with children & teens — younger children's personal boundaries
toddler-wont-hug-relatives.supports: Young children can be told it's their body and they can decide who hugs, kisses or tickles them, and that they can say no. Only this younger-children line is used; the rest of the page is about older kids and sexual consent and is not cited.

toddler-wont-hug-relatives.title: Why you shouldn't force the kids to hug Granny at Christmas
toddler-wont-hug-relatives.supports: 20 December 2018. Tell relatives in advance the child will choose the greeting; offer a choice (hug, high-five, fist-bump, wave); prepare the child that someone may ask; respect the answer; acknowledge the adult's disappointment.

toddler-wont-hug-relatives.title: Doctor's Orders: Your Kids Don't Have to Hug Anyone
toddler-wont-hug-relatives.supports: December 2025, a pediatrician author. Kids shouldn't be forced to show physical affection; respect over offending; a short line to the relative plus an alternative for the child, then move on. Cited once, as a secondary source.

instead-of-threats.title: Tips for Giving Directions — Essentials for Parenting Toddlers
instead-of-threats.supports: 30 April 2026. Tell the child what to do, not just what to stop; offer two choices; use a neutral tone; give one warning, then follow through; before naming a consequence, check that you have the time and energy to follow through.

instead-of-threats.title: Positive discipline for young children
instead-of-threats.publisher: Caring for Kids — Canadian Paediatric Society
instead-of-threats.supports: Last updated January 2020. Say what you mean, mean what you say, and follow through; use fewer words; tell children what they can do; talk to a health professional if the pattern is affecting the relationship.

instead-of-threats.title: What's the Best Way to Discipline My Child?
instead-of-threats.supports: Last updated 11/5/2018. Harsh verbal discipline and shaming are ineffective and harmful.

instead-of-threats.title: Parental wellbeing — stepping out of the anger cycle (Hebrew)
instead-of-threats.publisher: Israel Ministry of Health — parenting site
instead-of-threats.supports: 15 January 2025. Say what you will do to help the child keep the limit, and say what is allowed. Cited for meaning only.

time-out-vs-time-in.title: How to Give a Time-Out
time-out-vs-time-in.supports: Last updated 11/5/2018. One warning, name the behavior, a quiet place that is not the bedroom or playroom, one minute per year of age, return the child if they leave; from age 3 you can try “come back when you feel ready”; adults can take a time-out; time-outs can be used too much.

time-out-vs-time-in.title: How to Use Time-Out — Essentials for Parenting Toddlers
time-out-vs-time-in.supports: 30 April 2026. Use for dangerous, harmful or rule-breaking behavior, or not following a direction after one warning; one minute per year of age; no talking, looking or playing during; consider time-in when the child is in emotional distress. Curl returns 403 (bot block); content verified via fetch on 2026-11-10.

time-out-vs-time-in.title: Positive discipline techniques for kids under 5
time-out-vs-time-in.supports: 3 November 2026. For toddlers: redirection, routines, transition warnings and praise. For many toddlers, a time-in can work better than a time-out: staying close, helping them calm down and naming the feeling can teach more than sending them away alone. Does not ban time-out.

time-out-vs-time-in.title: Positive discipline for young children
time-out-vs-time-in.publisher: Caring for Kids — Canadian Paediatric Society
time-out-vs-time-in.supports: Last updated January 2020. Time-in as a connecting alternative; time-outs should not be used with children under the age of 3; time-out only after other positive methods.

time-out-vs-time-in.title: Are Timeouts Helpful or Harmful to Young Children?
time-out-vs-time-in.supports: Claire Lerner, 14 January 2016. An angry, shaming time-out can make things worse; a calm break can help when the child cannot accept comfort; children under 3 cannot be expected to reflect on what they did. Cited as the article; Lerner is not presented as someone who spoke to Kidsit.

time-out-vs-time-in.title: Disciplining Your Toddler
time-out-vs-time-in.supports: Date reviewed February 2023. A short time-out from positive attention for hitting, biting or throwing food; kitchen chair or bottom stair; about 1 minute per year of age, and 3–5 minutes is plenty; calmly return the child if they get up, without talking. The page also uses “time-in” to mean praise for good behavior — that definition was not borrowed.

toddler-refuses-bath.title: Fear of the bath: babies and toddlers
toddler-refuses-bath.supports: Toddlers may fear the drain noise, slipping, hair washing or soap in the eyes; there is no need to force a very upset child; a predictable routine helps; take the child out before pulling the plug; a bath cap or goggles can help; never leave the room.

toddler-refuses-bath.title: הילד מסרב להתקלח: תירוץ או בעיה בוויסות החושי?
toddler-refuses-bath.publisher: Hillel Yaffe Medical Center — occupational therapy service
toddler-refuses-bath.supports: 29 June 2023. Toddlers' refusal is often ordinary resistance; extreme, repeated distress despite a calm setup, together with other sensory signs (picky eating, noise sensitivity, avoiding sand or certain clothes), is worth an occupational-therapy consultation. A gentle rinse with a cup or hand is preferable to a strong shower stream.

toddler-refuses-bath.title: Hairwashing for children: tips and advice
toddler-refuses-bath.publisher: NHS Children and Family Health Devon
toddler-refuses-bath.supports: Bring water to the head with a jug, count the rinses, use a visor, goggles or flannel over the eyes, let the child lather themselves, and lean forward instead of back.

toddler-refuses-bath.title: Bathroom Safety
toddler-refuses-bath.supports: Last updated 1/24/2017. Never leave a young child alone in the bath, even for a moment.

toddler-refuses-bath.title: בטיחות ילדים במים וטביעות ילדים
toddler-refuses-bath.supports: 23 April 2026. Do not leave toddlers alone in the bath, even for a moment.

toddler-refuses-bath.title: רווחה הורית - לצאת ממעגל הכעס
toddler-refuses-bath.supports: 15 January 2025. A defined choice and play appear as ways out of a stand-off. Cited for that principle only; examples were not copied.

preschooler-lying.title: When Children Lie: What Parents Can Do
preschooler-lying.supports: Updated 18 March 2025. Children under about 6 often have difficulty telling fantasy from reality; harsh punishment is usually not effective; the parent's own honesty is the main teacher; persistent lying can be a sign that help is needed.

preschooler-lying.title: When Young Children Lie
preschooler-lying.supports: 13 February 2017. Very common for preschoolers; self-control still developing; fear of a reaction drives lying; don't ask if they did it when you already know — describe and offer a repair.

preschooler-lying.title: Children & lying
preschooler-lying.supports: Lying often starts around 2–3 and is more common at 4–6; praise the admission; don't label the child a liar; talk to a professional if lying is constant with other worrying behavior, or if the child seems afraid to tell you something or may be covering for someone.

preschooler-lying.title: Why Kids Lie and What Parents Can Do About It
preschooler-lying.supports: Last reviewed or updated 12 February 2026. Avoid labeling a child a liar. Use only the avoid-labeling and occasional-versus-persistent points; most of the page is about older children. Curl can return 403 (bot block); content verified via fetch on 2026-11-12.

preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.title: What happened today?
preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.supports: Early-years activity, birth to 5. Make time at the end of the day to talk; give the child time to think and respond; mix open and closed questions; make a routine for catching up (for example dinner or bath time).

preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.title: Talking & listening activities: 3–6 years
preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.supports: Talk whenever you're together; a special place or time each day (for example after getting into bed).

preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.title: Improving Family Communications
preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.supports: Updated 15 December 2025. Undivided attention; turn off the TV; be a good listener; ask about feelings; repeat back what you heard.

preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.title: Selective Mutism
preschooler-wont-talk-about-day.supports: Last reviewed 1 May 2026. Closing box only: a child who talks freely at home but not at all at gan for more than a month (not counting the first month of a new setting), and it gets in the way of playing or joining in — start by talking to your doctor. Do not name a diagnosis on the page. HTTP 200 on 2026-11-12.
